name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,837

clue.text: Having issue with hearth, cooked boring meal (10)

indicators.note: What comes out of the pan is not in the state it went in, so the letters are served up rearranged.
To bore is to drill into something, and what does the drilling ends up inside it.

blocks.note: food is a meal, and it opens after its first letter to take the filling
the six letters of HEARTH in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has trouble with the fireplace and ends up cooking a dull dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having issue' is the legal sense of issue, meaning offspring, so the domestic row the surface offers is a decoy. 'Cooked' and 'boring' are two separate instructions, not one.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatherhood is the state of having children, and issue is the old legal word for offspring that wills and crosswords keep alive.

clue.text: Seafood close to sea bass and sole (7)

indicators.note: The close of anything is its end, so what is wanted is the letter that ends the word.

blocks.note: the last letter of SEA
b is the musical abbreviation for bass
sole means alone, the only one

explanation.surface: A fishmonger lists what came in today, alongside sea bass and sole.
explanation.walkthrough: Bass and sole are both fish, which is exactly why neither is a fish here: one is the singing voice, the other is the 'only' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible sea snail, prized on the plate from California to Japan, so seafood is the class it belongs to.

clue.text: Henry put on pretty dress (5)

indicators.note: Putting one thing on another sets it above, and in a down entry whatever sits above is written first.

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
'pretty tired' and 'a bit tired' say the same thing, so pretty = A BIT

explanation.surface: Henry gets himself up in an attractive frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like a man and is a unit of measurement, the way 'volt' or 'watt' would be. The dress is the one a monk or nun wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is the plain robe worn by a monk or a nun, so dress is clothing in its general sense.

clue.text: Racecourse favourite gets VIP treatment (3,6)

blocks.note: Redcar is a racecourse in the seaside town of that name in North Yorkshire
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: At the races the favourite is treated like visiting royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing surface hides a place name, and English courses turn up constantly in clues: Ascot, Epsom, Aintree, Redcar. 'Favourite' looks like the betting sense and means the pampered one.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out the red carpet is what a host does for an important guest, so the phrase stands for the whole star welcome.

clue.text: Somewhat friendly pranks seeming to upset (2,8,5)

indicators.note: Upsetting something tips it over and spills its contents out in a fresh arrangement.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

explanation.surface: Practical jokes that look as though they are about to cause real trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The little word 'to' belongs to the letters, not to the instruction, which is where a long anagram like this one usually goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: People on speaking terms are civil to each other and no warmer than that, which is the work 'somewhat' is doing.

clue.text: Things said at police getting twisted (5)

indicators.note: Something twisted round has been turned to face the other way, so the letters are read backwards.

blocks.note: taken as it stands
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of a British police force

explanation.surface: Statements made at the police station come out distorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' promises distorted testimony and delivers a backwards reading. Dicta is the plural of dictum, familiar from the obiter dicta of law reports.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictum is a pronouncement — Latin for a thing said — so dicta are things said, several of them.

clue.text: Band of elite soldiers back on warpath (4)

indicators.note: The back of a word is its rear end, which is its final letter.

blocks.note: the SAS, the Special Air Service, is the British army's elite regiment
the final letter of WARPATH

explanation.surface: Crack troops are on the warpath once again.
explanation.walkthrough: A sash is part of ceremonial uniform, so the soldiering fits the answer as well as it fits the wordplay. 'Back' asks for one letter here and is not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn round the waist or across one shoulder, which is 'band' in its plainest sense.

clue.text: Bog went by water on map, near delta (9)

indicators.note: In a down entry one thing sits on another by being written above it, so the swimming goes in first.

blocks.note: to travel by water under your own power is to swim; the past tense is SWAM
a plan is a scale drawing or map of a place
delta is D in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A route is plotted by water, close to the delta shown on the map.
explanation.walkthrough: A river delta really is marshy ground, so the geography of the surface sits next door to the answer; the clue means only the radio-alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Swampland and bog both name ground so waterlogged that it will not carry a footstep, so the two are straight synonyms.

clue.text: Special festival's back with yen to spend extravagantly (7)

indicators.note: A word's back is its tail end, so what is handed over is its last letter.

blocks.note: sp is the standard short form of special
the last letter of FESTIVAL
a yen for something is an urge for it

explanation.surface: A one-off festival has come round again and there is money to burn.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'festival's back' to mean the festival has returned; the wordplay reads it as a possessive. 'Yen' is the appetite, not the currency, which would have handed over a lone Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to lay money out freely on something indulgent, which is spending extravagantly under another name.

clue.text: Spotted flatfish at bottom of river (6)

blocks.note: a dab is a small flatfish of the plaice family
the bottom of a river is its bed

explanation.surface: A flatfish is sighted lying on the riverbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom of' normally asks for a final letter, so the R of 'river' is the trap; the setter wants the whole riverbed instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To dab paint on is to apply it in small spots, so a surface that has been dabbed has been spotted.

clue.text: Warm fur coats start to outsell cold one (8)

indicators.note: A coat goes right round what it covers, so the fur closes round the letters it is given.
The start of a word is the letter it opens with.

blocks.note: sable is the dark fur of the marten of that name
the first letter of OUTSELL
c is cold, the marking on a tap
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: In a coat shop, warm fur is beginning to outsell something lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coats' looks like the garments the shop is selling and is in fact the verb, and what it wraps round is three unrelated single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sociable person is warm in the friendly sense, the warmth of good company rather than of temperature.

clue.text: Stole evidence in Oxbridge row? (4,4)

blocks.note: a boa is a long stole of fur or feathers worn round the neck
a trace of something is the evidence it leaves behind

explanation.surface: Someone made off with the proof during a university rowing contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' is the garment rather than the theft the sentence sets up. The question mark is doing real work: the answer is one particular row, not rows in general.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford against Cambridge contest on the Thames, so the definition names it by example, with row in its rowing sense.

clue.text: Hope is a small, quiet emotion (6)

blocks.note: taken as it stands
s is the clothing size small
p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
ire is anger, one emotion among many

explanation.surface: Hope painted as a small, quiet feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes hope sound like a modest little emotion, which hides the fact that the answer is a verb: something you do rather than something you have.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to hope for something and reach towards it, so the verb 'hope' drops straight into its place.

clue.text: Betray group of spies as dictator (4)

indicators.note: A dictator is someone saying words out loud for another to write down, so this word is heard rather than spelt.

blocks.note: a cell is a small group of agents working together, and said aloud it gives the answer

explanation.surface: A ring of spies is handed over to the tyrant in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' is the person dictating words for someone else to take down, not the tyrant the spy story suggests. Sound and spelling differ by a single letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell someone is to betray them for your own advantage, as in selling out a friend.

clue.text: Eleventh-hour comeback using creative thinking (9)

blocks.note: an eleventh-hour decision is a late one
a side that rallies stages a comeback

explanation.surface: A team leaves it to the last minute and then stages a recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comeback' looks like an instruction to reverse and is nothing of the sort, being the sporting recovery. Lateral thinking is Edward de Bono's term for attacking a problem from the side.
explanation.definitionFit: To work laterally is to come at a problem sideways instead of head-on, which is what creative thinking means here.

clue.text: Bluffer's expression perfect when holding decent card (5,4)

indicators.note: To hold something is to keep it inside you, so the holding letters close round the held ones.

blocks.note: perf is the grammarian's short form of perfect, as in the perfect tense
OK means decent, good enough
an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: A card player gives nothing away while sitting on a strong hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' is the poker word the surface leans on and the container instruction underneath it. PERF is the abbreviation grammar books use for the perfect tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker face is the blank look worn so that nobody can read the hand behind it, which is exactly what a bluffer needs.

clue.text: Runner smuggles ketamine and ecstasy for dodgy dealer (9)

indicators.note: Smuggling is carrying goods concealed inside, so what is smuggled sits within the carrier's letters.

blocks.note: a racer is a runner
ket is the street name for ketamine
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: An athlete carries drugs on behalf of a shady supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug-squad surface does the misdirecting: a runner there is a courier, while the wordplay wants nothing but plain athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer lives off organised crime — extortion, protection, black-market trade — so 'dodgy dealer' catches the crooked line of business.

clue.text: In a stupor, Tom perhaps needs a pick-me-up (9)

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat, and 'perhaps' flags one example of the general word
taken as it stands
a tonic is a pick-me-up

explanation.surface: A listless cat called Tom could do with something to perk him up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom perhaps' is the crossword way of pointing at a cat through one of them. The stupor is the cat's in the surface and a clinical condition in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone catatonic is rigid and unresponsive, the stupor being the psychiatric state the word names.

clue.text: Directs Rocky titles (7)

indicators.note: Rocky ground is uneven and unsteady, and letters on unsteady footing will not keep their order.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: Somebody directs the film Rocky.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics dress 'Rocky' up as a film title and stand it beside 'Directs' as though both belonged to cinema, while its real job is to unsettle those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A film's credits are the lists of names that roll at either end of it, known in the trade as the titles.

clue.text: Couple performing outstanding tango (4)

blocks.note: a bill still outstanding is one that is due
tango is T in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A pair dance a magnificent tango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' is the accountant's word here, meaning unpaid, rather than the praise the dancers are being offered.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet is a piece written for two performers, so a couple performing together are giving one.

clue.text: Beheaded queens wrongly over sex in private washroom (2,5)

indicators.note: Beheading takes off the head, and a word's head is the letter it begins with.
Letters set down wrongly are letters in the wrong order.
One thing laid over another covers it, so these letters close round what they cover.

blocks.note: QUEENS loses its head, the Q, and the five letters left are rearranged
'it' is the coy old word for sex

explanation.surface: Queens are wrongly executed over a sex scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beheaded' reads as Tudor history next to 'queens', which is the trap; it is the ordinary instruction to drop a first letter. 'It' for sex is old slang that crosswords keep in circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: An en suite is a bathroom opening straight off one bedroom and used by whoever sleeps there, so it is private by design.

clue.text: Pointillist surfaces on some unfamiliar art (6)

indicators.note: The surfaces of a thing are its outsides, so each word gives up the letters on its outside.

blocks.note: the outside letters of SOME
the outside letters of UNFAMILIAR
the outside letters of ART

explanation.surface: A pointillist's painted surfaces turn up on a piece of art nobody recognises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surfaces' looks like the noun a painter works on, canvas and board, and is asking instead for the outside of each word after it. Seurat built his pictures from dots of pure colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Seurat invented pointillism, so the word for the technique names him by the method he worked in.

clue.text: He sings relatively high note for audience (5)

definitions.note: The definition describes the man instead of naming him: the singer whose voice sits relatively high is a tenor.

indicators.note: Anything done for an audience is meant to be heard, so the word is spoken rather than written.

blocks.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note in Britain, and said aloud it gives the answer

explanation.surface: A singer holds a high note in front of a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is the banknote and not the musical one, which is the trap in a clue otherwise full of singing. Tenor and tenner are all but identical in most English accents.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is the high male voice, pitched above the baritone and bass, so a man singing up there is one.

clue.text: Nancy's very flirtatious act causes offence (8)

blocks.note: Nancy is a city in France, so the word wanted is the French très
to make a pass at someone is to make a flirtatious advance

explanation.surface: A forward piece of flirting in Nancy leaves somebody insulted.
explanation.walkthrough: A French place name in a clue is usually telling you to change language, and Nancy's word for 'very' is très.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespass is a wrongdoing, the sense kept alive in 'forgive us our trespasses' alongside the land-law meaning.

clue.text: On the counter is energy drink (5)

indicators.note: To run counter to something is to go the opposite way, so these letters are read in the opposite direction.

blocks.note: taken as it stands
pep is energy, vigour

explanation.surface: Something energising is standing on the shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' plays on the counter a bottle stands on and on over-the-counter goods, while its real job is to turn the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepsi is a brand of cola, so the definition names the class the trade name belongs to.

clue.text: Military ship worker who might deal with Green Berets (8)

definitions.text: worker who might deal with Green Berets

blocks.note: mil is the everyday short form of military
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A crewman on a warship has dealings with the US special forces.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital letters are free in a surface, and these two turn hats into a regiment. Everything before 'worker' is the wordplay, everything after it is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A milliner makes and sells hats, so green berets are stock in the shop rather than the American special forces the capitals suggest.

clue.text: Dash of medium strength liquor ultimately vermouth (6)

indicators.note: What comes ultimately is what comes last, so the word gives up its final letter.

blocks.note: a medium's claimed strength is ESP, extrasensory perception
the last letter of LIQUOR
It is Italian vermouth, the It of a gin and It

explanation.surface: A measure of middling spirits is finished off with vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface is a drinks order, which is why 'medium' reads as a strength; the medium wanted is the one at the seance. Gin and It was the fashionable cocktail of the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is the French word English borrowed for wit and liveliness, and dash is that same spirit and flair.

clue.text: Upsilon and psi reversed in guessing game (1-3)

indicators.note: Reversed means turned back to front, so the letters are read from the far end.

blocks.note: upsilon is the Greek letter English writes as Y
the Greek letter psi, spelt out in full

explanation.surface: Two Greek letters written down back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: Greek letters go into wordplay in either of two ways, and this clue uses both: upsilon as the single letter it stands for, psi as its name spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: I-spy is the children's guessing game — 'I spy with my little eye' — where one player gives a letter and the rest guess the object.

clue.text: Checked others showered (10)

blocks.note: the rest of a group is the others
it showered and it rained say the same thing of the weather

explanation.surface: Someone checked that everybody else had washed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bathroom reading of 'showered' is the trap, and the answer needs the weather one instead. Three words are all the setter gives you here.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or curb it — a temper checked, a horse checked — which is what restrained means.
